question.text: An offshore Cayman master fund wants to appoint Mr. Vikram Shah, India-based, as its fund manager without triggering a 'business connection' / POEM risk for the offshore fund. Which ITA provision offers a safe harbour, and which is a KEY condition?

answer.text: Section 115UB — India-resident sponsor must hold < 20% units

Section 9A — among other conditions: the eligible investment fund must have at least 25 members, India-resident investors' aggregate participation must not exceed 5%, and the fund manager must be remunerated at arm's length

explanation.text: The Logic: Section 9A of the Income-tax Act is the safe-harbour provision for offshore "Eligible Investment Funds" advised by an India-based "Eligible Fund Manager". When the prescribed conditions are met, the activity of the India-based manager does not, by itself, create a business connection or treat the offshore fund as Indian-resident. Among the listed conditions are a minimum number of investors (commonly cited as 25 members) with no concentration, a low cap on aggregate participation by India-resident investors, arm's-length remuneration to the fund manager, and the fund not carrying on business in India beyond its investment activities. The Trap: Section 115UB (A) is the Cat I/II AIF pass-through provision and does not govern offshore manager safe-harbour. Section 90(2) (C) is the treaty-benefit selection rule, not a business-connection carve-out. Section 194LBA (D) is a TDS section for business-trust (REIT/InvIT) distributions. Note: The Section 9A safe-harbour framework, its specific eligible-fund and eligible-fund-manager conditions, and any related GIFT-City alternative framing are not explicitly developed in the cited workbook chapter (FINAL_Series-XIX-C_AIF Managers_Ver-Dec-2025.pdf, pp. 446-484, 521), which focuses on AIF-specific taxation. The framing above is general Indian tax-law knowledge under the Income-tax Act.
